chain.label: ABX had no formal FEF program, guidelines, limitations or FEF pilot training requirements
chain.trigger: the failure of ABX to establish a formal functional evaluation flight program that included adequate program guidelines, requirements and pilot training for performance of these flights

chain.label: Crew's only DC-8 stall experience was in a simulator with no stall break; neither pilot had stalled the actual airplane
chain.trigger: neither pilot involved in the accident had performed the clean stall maneuver in a DC-8 airplane before the accident flight

caused_by.evidence: Training for FEFs was informal and undocumented, and ABX had established no specific training or proficiency requirements for pilots conducting FEFs

chain.label: Stall warning (stick shaker) system inoperative, undetected by preflight or maintenance checks
chain.trigger: Given the extreme angles of attack that were eventually attained prior to impact, the stall warning system clearly was inoperative

chain.label: Mountainous terrain beneath the evaluation flight route near Narrows, Virginia
chain.trigger: The airplane wreckage was found on the southeast side of a 4,200-foot mountain at the 3,400-foot level

chain.label: Crew continued the FEF and its stall series after dark following repeated maintenance delays
chain.trigger: the crew had originally scheduled a 1320 departure. However, the airplane departed GSO at 1740, following maintenance delays

caused_by.evidence: ABX had no specific prohibition against conducting an FEF at night ... no requirements were established by ABX for ambient lighting conditions, visual references, or distance from cloud tops

chain.label: No visible natural horizon: darkness with cloud layers above and just below the maneuver altitude
chain.trigger: the flightcrew did not have a clearly visible natural horizon because of darkness and clouds above and below the airplane

caused_by.evidence: The accident occurred during the hours of darkness

chain.label: Airplane decelerated into a full clean stall at 126 knots during the FEF stall series
chain.trigger: a Safety Board performance study based on FDR data indicated that the pre-stall buffet began at 149 knots and that the stall occurred at 126 knots

caused_by.evidence: The evaluation flight profile form that the flightcrew was using for the FEF required that the flightcrew identify and record the speed at which the stick shaker activated and the speed of the stall indication

chain.label: Stick shaker failed to activate before or during the full stall
chain.trigger: that's a stall right there... ain't no [stick] shaker

caused_by.evidence: the Safety Board is concerned that the stick shaker failed to activate at any time during the full stall that followed ... the Safety Board was unable to identify the failure mode of the stall warning system

chain.label: PF held and increased aft control column pressure throughout the stall recovery attempt
chain.trigger: the PF applied inappropriate control column back pressure during the stall recovery attempt in an inadequate performance of the stall recovery procedure

caused_by.evidence: For 8 seconds following the initiation of the stall recovery, from 1808:13 through 1808:21, the PF maintained the airplane's pitch attitude at between 10 degrees and 14 degrees ANU

the flightcrew's exposure to a low fidelity reproduction of the DC-8's stall characteristics in the ABX DC-8 flight training simulator was a factor in the PF holding aft (stall-inducing) control column inputs when the airplane began to pitch down and roll
the inoperative stall warning system contributed to the accident by failing to reinforce to the flightcrew the indications that the airplane was in a full stall during the recovery attempt
by conducting these maneuvers without a visible natural horizon, the flightcrew was deprived of an important flight attitude reference that would have aided in their recovery from a full stall

chain.label: No. 2 engine compressor surges at high angle of attack, followed by asymmetric power reduction
chain.trigger: the CVR recorded sounds similar to engine compressor surges (popping sounds) that continued for 9 seconds

caused_by.evidence: The engine compressor surges that began at 1808:20 (as a result of the disruption of air flow though the No. 2 engine at the prevailing high angle of attack)

chain.label: PNF, acting as pilot-in-command and instructor, failed to correct the PF's inputs or take control
chain.trigger: the PNF's failure, as the pilot-in-command, to recognize, address and correct the PF's inappropriate control inputs were causal to this accident

caused_by.evidence: when the PF did not respond adequately, the PNF did not escalate his verbal interventions or take over the controls ... the PNF never told the PF to move the control column forward
the engine compressor surges in the No. 2 engine (caused by airflow disruption) may have distracted the flightcrew during the critical early period of the stall recovery
if the flightcrew had received the expected cues from the stick shaker ... the PNF would have received a stronger signal to intervene
the PNF's instructional role, like his command role, was informal on this flight. Therefore, his command and instructional authority may have remained unclear

chain.label: Airplane held in a sustained stall through four roll reversals in a steep uncontrolled descent
chain.trigger: the airplane remained in an aerodynamic stall condition because the PF held significant back pressure on the control column all the way to impact

caused_by.evidence: Each time the airplane developed a large nose-down pitch rate ... the PF responded with additional back pressure
he apparently lost awareness of the flight's descent rate and proximity to the ground

chain.label: Impact with mountainous terrain at 3,400 feet msl at more than 240 knots
chain.trigger: The airplane struck mountainous terrain in a 52-degree, left wing low and 26-degree, nose-down attitude about 3,400 feet msl

caused_by.evidence: The sound of impact was recorded on the CVR at 1809:38, 3 seconds after the GPWS aural warning
impacted mountainous terrain in the vicinity of Narrows, Virginia

chain.label: All six occupants fatally injured; airplane destroyed by impact and postcrash fire
chain.trigger: The three flightcrew members and three maintenance/avionics technicians on board were fatally injured. The airplane was destroyed by the impact and a postcrash fire
